name: Cape Coast Castle and the Old Town
tagline: The white fort above the fishing beach
description: The historic core around the castle, a UNESCO site where enslaved people were held before the Atlantic crossing, with the dungeons and the Door of No Return preserved. Below it the fishing beach is a working one, packed with painted canoes. The old town streets behind hold colonial-era buildings in mixed repair.
bestFor: Anyone whose reason for being here is the castle and the history
pros: The castle and the museum at the door
The working fishing beach and its boats
Everything in the old town walkable
cons: The area is emotionally heavy to live beside
Busy with visitors and school groups

name: Pedu and the University Area
tagline: Around the University of Cape Coast, students and cheaper rents
description: The northern district built around the university campus, with student hostels, cheap chop bars, printing shops and a young population. It is where most of the town's foreign students and researchers live, where rents are lowest, and where English is most consistently spoken outside the tourist sites.
bestFor: Budget stays and anyone attached to the university
pros: The lowest rents in the town
Cheap student food and a young population
The most accessible social world for a newcomer
cons: Twenty minutes from the castle and the coast

name: Elmina (12 km west)
tagline: The older castle and a bigger fishing fleet
description: A separate town twenty minutes west with St George's Castle, built by the Portuguese in 1482 and the oldest European building in sub-Saharan Africa, plus a fishing harbour packed with hundreds of canoes that is one of the more extraordinary sights on this coast. Quieter and cheaper than Cape Coast.
bestFor: Stays that want the older castle and the fishing harbour
pros: St George's Castle and Fort St Jago
cons: Twenty minutes from Cape Coast's services
The harbour is pungent, which is the nature of it

name: Brimsu and the Northern Suburbs
tagline: Residential Cape Coast, away from the sea
description: The inland residential districts spreading north, with ordinary Ghanaian family compounds, local markets and schools, and a population that has nothing to do with tourism. It is where rents are lowest for a house rather than a room, and where the everyday life of the town happens.
bestFor: Long stays wanting a house at local prices
pros: Houses rather than rooms, at low rents
Local markets and genuine local pricing
cons: Away from the sea and the historic quarter
Power cuts and water interruptions are common

name: Kakum and the Forest Road (30 km north)
description: The road north into Kakum National Park, where a canopy walkway of rope bridges runs forty metres up through primary rainforest, which is the region's best-known attraction and genuinely worth the visit. A few lodges operate near the gate. It is green, cooler than the coast and entirely rural.
bestFor: Short stays in the forest rather than an urban base
pros: Kakum's canopy walkway and forest trails
Cooler and greener than the coast
cons: Half an hour from Cape Coast and transport is awkward
Accommodation is limited to a few lodges
